Internal free fermions in a four-dimensional bosonic string (4+Nf​/2−26=0)

Words: 169 Articles: 1
Bosonic string theory OurBigBook.com
Keeping the ordinary reparameterization bc ghost system, four embedding bosons require 44 additional real chiral fermions in each chirality to cancel the worldsheet Weyl anomaly. These are internal matter fields, not an assumed locally supersymmetric RNS construction. Their bilinear currents generate the chiral so(44) current algebra, with (244​)=946 currents. A full closed fermionic model also requires consistent spin-structure and modular projections; the central-charge count alone does not determine these choices.

Zero- and two-fermion vertices of an internally fermionized bosonic string (M2=−4/α′, −2/α′, 0)

Words: 103
Internal free fermions in a four-dimensional bosonic string OurBigBook.com
In the unprojected polynomial Neveu–Schwarz vertex sector, zero fermion insertions give the usual closed-string tachyon and the massless graviton, two-form and dilaton. Two insertions split into a left-right pair ψiψˉ​jeipX of internal weights (1/2,1/2) and a same-chirality current pair of weight one. The first has M2=−2/α′ and 44-squared scalar components. The second requires a bosonic derivative on the opposite side for level matching and gives the two sets of 946 massless gauge vectors. Four-fermion scalar-current products belong to a different insertion count. A chosen global projection may retain a subset, so these operators do not by themselves specify a projected string spectrum.

Open string

Words: 570 Articles: 11
Bosonic string theory OurBigBook.com
An open string has a worldsheet with boundary. Its endpoint conditions may be Neumann boundary conditions, Dirichlet boundary conditions, or mixtures selected independently in target-space directions.

Open-string oscillator degeneracy (F(w)=∏n≥1​(1−wn)−24)

Words: 96 Articles: 1
Open string OurBigBook.com
For an ordinary critical open string with all Neumann boundary conditions, there are 24 independent transverse creation oscillators at each positive mode number n. Summing their nonnegative occupation numbers gives one factor (1−wn)−24. The coefficient dp​=[wp]F(w) counts oscillator polarizations at level p, excluding continuous center-of-mass momentum and additional endpoint multiplicities. Cauchy coefficient formula gives dp​=(2πi)−1∮F(w)w−p−1dw.

Large-level degeneracy of an open bosonic string (dp​∼2−1/2p−27/4e4πp​)

Words: 42
Open-string oscillator degeneracy OurBigBook.com
The Dedekind eta function modular transformation gives F(e−t)∼(t/2π)12exp(4π2/t−t). The saddle-point approximation for coefficient extraction has t0​=2π/p−1​, phase 4πp−1​ and curvature (p−1)3/2/π. Its prefactor t012​ supplies (p−1)−6 and the Gaussian width supplies (p−1)−3/4/2​. This explains both the exponential growth and the power −27/4.

Open-string endpoint momentum flux (Jm​=eT2Xm′​+uPm​)

Words: 162 Articles: 3
Open string OurBigBook.com
For the Nambu-Goto phase-space action, P˙m​=∂σ​Jm​ with Jm​=eT2Xm′​+uPm​. Thus P˙m​=Jm​(π)−Jm​(0). Free endpoint variations force Jm​=0 individually. A Dirichlet boundary condition allows an external support or D-brane to absorb momentum in the fixed direction.

Variational open-string boundary conditions (Jm​δXm∣∂Σ​=0)

Words: 59
Open-string endpoint momentum flux OurBigBook.com
The spatial integration-by-parts term in the Nambu-Goto phase-space action pairs endpoint displacement with momentum flux Jm​=eT2Xm′​+uPm​. Free endpoint displacements require zero flux. Fixed normal coordinates instead set those variations to zero, while tangential variations retain a Neumann boundary condition. Boundary conditions must also be preserved by the equations of motion. In a boundary-preserving gauge with u=0, mixed Neumann boundary conditions and Dirichlet boundary conditions implement a planar D-brane.

Free-end string boundary condition (X′m∣∂Σ​=0)

Words: 71 Articles: 1
Open-string endpoint momentum flux OurBigBook.com
Free endpoint variations set the open string flux eT2Xm′​+uPm​ to zero. In a boundary-adapted temporal gauge, freedom to vary time forces u=0 at the end. Nonzero lapse then gives X′m=0, a Neumann boundary condition.
Null motion of a free string endpoint (X˙2∣∂Σ​=0)
Words: 40
Free-end string boundary condition OurBigBook.com
In a boundary-adapted temporal gauge, a free open string endpoint has X′m=0. The Nambu–Goto phase-space constraints then imply P2=0, while X˙=eP implies X˙2=0. For X0=t, its spatial speed is one. This null boundary is compatible with a timelike interior worldsheet.

Open-string mode expansion

Words: 290 Articles: 4
Open string OurBigBook.com
In conformal gauge, a free open-string coordinate with Neumann boundary conditions has a cosine expansion. Canonical quantization turns its nonzero Fourier coefficients into string oscillators.

Integer-mode expansion with parallel D-brane endpoints (cosnσ for NN,sinnσ for DD)

Words: 62
Open-string mode expansion OurBigBook.com
On 0≤σ≤π, a coordinate with Neumann boundary conditions at both ends has a constant position, linear time zero mode and cosine oscillators. A coordinate with Dirichlet boundary conditions at both ends has a linear spatial interpolation between endpoint positions and sine oscillators, with no momentum zero mode. Both have integer frequencies. This differs from an ND boundary condition, which applies different conditions at the two ends of the same coordinate and gives half-integer frequencies.

Oscillator symplectic form of an open string ({αjm​,αkn​}=−ijηmnδj+k,0​)

Words: 46
Open-string mode expansion OurBigBook.com
The Fourier kinetic term ∑k>0​iα−k​⋅α˙k​/k supplies conjugate pairs, with α−k​=αk∗​. Inverting its symplectic form yields the displayed Poisson brackets. Nonzero modes are independent of the center-of-mass pair, while α0​=2α′​p is the momentum zero mode. The imaginary factors are compatible with a real action up to a total derivative.

Neumann-Dirichlet open-string boundary condition (∂σ​X(0)=0,X(π)=y)

Words: 162 Articles: 1
Open-string mode expansion OurBigBook.com
A transverse open string coordinate has an ND boundary condition when one endpoint obeys a Neumann boundary condition and the other a Dirichlet boundary condition. On a strip of width π, its nonconstant spatial eigenfunctions are cos((n+1/2)σ) when the free endpoint is at zero. They solve the endpoint equations because their derivatives vanish at zero and their values vanish at π. Reversing the endpoints gives sine eigenfunctions with the same frequencies. The fixed endpoint removes the dynamical worldsheet zero mode.
Bosonic ND boundary-changing conformal weight (hND​=1/16)
Words: 91
Neumann-Dirichlet open-string boundary condition OurBigBook.com
For one free boson, the mixed ND open-string sector has strip vacuum energy E0​=1/48. The strip-to-plane transformation relates this energy to the plane Virasoro algebra zero mode by E0​=h−c/24, with central charge c=1. Hence its ground conformal weight is h=1/48+1/24=1/16. For d independent ND coordinates the weights add to d/16. At d=24, the plane matter ground weight is 3/2, while the strip oscillator vacuum energy is 1/2. The plane physical condition L0plane​−1=0 is therefore equivalent to α′p∥2​+N+1/2=0. The apparent different constants are coordinate/constraint conventions, not different mass spectra.

Closed string

Words: 115 Articles: 2
Bosonic string theory OurBigBook.com
A closed string has a cylindrical worldsheet without boundary. Periodicity permits independent left- and right-moving oscillator sectors and, in a compact target direction, winding modes.

Large-level degeneracy of a closed bosonic string (gN​∼21​(N−1)−27/2e8πN−1​)

Words: 70
Closed string OurBigBook.com
The left and right transverse oscillator sectors each have generating function ∏m≥1​(1−qm)−24. Its coefficient satisfies dN​∼2−1/2(N−1)−27/4e4πN−1​. Closed-string level matching requires equal levels but leaves their polarizations independent, so gN​=dN2​. With α′M2=4(N−1), the exponential is eβH​M with βH​=4πα′​. The smooth rest-mass density is proportional to M−26eβH​M, since dN/dM=α′M/2. This distinguishes degeneracy per level from density per unit mass. The polynomial prefactor matters at the boundary of canonical convergence.

Closed-string mode expansion

Words: 20
Closed string OurBigBook.com
A free closed-string embedding coordinate is the sum of center-of-mass zero modes and independent periodic left- and right-moving oscillator expansions.

Covariant quantization of the bosonic string

Words: 590 Articles: 13
Bosonic string theory OurBigBook.com
Covariant quantization keeps target-spacetime Lorentz covariance manifest, imposes canonical commutation relations on every embedding coordinate and removes unphysical states with the Virasoro constraints.

No-ghost theorem below the critical bosonic dimension (2≤d≤26,a=1)

Words: 97
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
For integer target dimension 2≤d≤26, intercept a=1 and ordinary nonzero momentum, the old covariant string quantization conditions leave a positive-semidefinite physical inner product. Quotienting its physical null string states removes gauge degeneracy. A DDF operator basis displays d−2 positive transverse oscillators; below dimension 26 the remaining physical longitudinal sector can be organized as a unitary Virasoro algebra sector with central charge 26−d and highest weight zero. At d=26 this extra sector becomes null and the quotient reduces to the 24 transverse oscillators. The result concerns negative-norm states, not the removal of the bosonic tachyon, and it does not itself cancel the worldsheet Weyl anomaly of a subcritical matter theory.

DDF operator ([Ami​,Anj​]=mδijδm+n,0​)

Words: 104
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
DDF operators are transverse physical string oscillators constructed as contour integrals of weight-one string vertex operators. Choose a null reference momentum q and transverse polarizations ϵi​ orthogonal to it and to a reference on-shell momentum. The integrand is proportional to ϵi​⋅∂Xeinq⋅X; its normalization and q⋅p are fixed so the operators obey the oscillator algebra in the title and commute with the positive-mode Virasoro constraints. For an open-string tachyon seed, one can use 2α′q⋅p=1. Acting with negative modes shifts momentum and raises oscillator level while preserving the physical mass-shell condition. Their transverse Fock space has positive norm and makes the physical content of the no-ghost theorem for the critical bosonic string explicit.

No-ghost theorem for the critical bosonic string

Words: 58
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
In flat 26-dimensional bosonic string theory, at ordinary nonzero momentum, take physical string states satisfying Ln>0​∣ψ⟩=0 and (L0​−1)∣ψ⟩=0. The inner product restricted to these states is positive semidefinite. Quotienting by physical null string states removes the degeneracy; the resulting Hilbert space is represented by the 24 transverse string oscillators. This is a statement about negative-norm matter states, not about removing the auxiliary Faddeev-Popov ghosts. It does not remove the bosonic tachyon.

Level-two open-string polarization decomposition (ζμν​=20t​(3qμ​qν​+ημν​)+qμ​Aν​+qν​Aμ​+cμν​)

Words: 59
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
For d=26, q2=−2 and the physical string state [ζμν​α−1μ​α−1ν​+bμ​α−2μ​]∣p⟩, the Virasoro constraints give bν​=−qμζμν​ and t=ζμμ​=−2q⋅b. Every solution has the displayed decomposition, where q⋅A=0 and c is symmetric, traceless and transverse to q. The vector piece is L−1​(2A⋅α−1​∣p⟩); the scalar piece is t(L−2​+3L−12​/2)∣p⟩/10. These are null string states, leaving the transverse traceless massive tensor as the physical polarization.

Negative-norm string state

Words: 27
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
Time-coordinate oscillators produce negative norms in the covariant indefinite Fock space. A physical negative-norm state would violate probabilistic unitarity. Such ghosts differ from the anticommuting worldsheet ghost fields introduced by gauge fixing.

Old covariant string quantization ((L0​−a)∣ψ⟩=0,Ln>0​∣ψ⟩=0)

Words: 98 Articles: 2
Covariant quantization of the bosonic string OurBigBook.com
Old covariant quantization retains all target-space string oscillators and imposes (L0​−a)∣ψ⟩=0 and Ln​∣ψ⟩=0 for n>0. Negative-mode constraints are adjoints, not further annihilation conditions. Quotienting physical null string states removes redundant polarizations.

Level-two scalar in covariant string quantization (⟨S∣S⟩=252​(D−1)(26−D))

Words: 39
Old covariant string quantization OurBigBook.com
At a=1, let k=2α′​p, k2=−2. The physical scalar [α−1​⋅α−1​+(D+4)(k⋅α−1​)2/10+(D−1)k⋅α−2​/5]∣p⟩ has norm 2(D−1)(26−D)/25. It is positive below 26, null at 26, and a string ghost state above 26. Matching the ordinary transverse spectrum removes this extra scalar at 26.

Level-one intercept bound in covariant string quantization (a≤1)

Words: 32
Old covariant string quantization OurBigBook.com
A polarization obeys p⋅ϵ=0 and p2=(a−1)/α′. If a>1, spacelike momentum allows a negative-norm timelike polarization. Thus ghost absence requires a≤1. At a=1 the null string state identification ϵ∼ϵ+λp leaves D−2 polarizations.

A physical string state obeys the Virasoro mass-shell and positive-mode constraints. States differing by a null state represent the same physical polarization.

Null-state quotient of a string (Hphys​/radHphys​)
Words: 38
Null string state OurBigBook.com
The physical state space of old covariant quantization is quotiented by its physical spurious states, which are orthogonal to all physical states. In a ghost-free sector these form the radical of the semidefinite inner product. The quotient retains positive physical polarizations.
Level-two scalar Virasoro null state (∣Z⟩=(L−2​+23​L−12​)∣p⟩)
Words: 29
Null string state OurBigBook.com
For L0​∣p⟩=−∣p⟩, the descendant Z=(L−2​+23​L−12​)∣p⟩ obeys L1​Z=0 and L2​Z=(D−26)∣p⟩/2. It becomes physical and null at 26 and supplies the scalar quotient needed for the massive spin-two light-cone gauge in string theory spectrum.

Bosonic string theory OurBigBook.com
String tension is energy per unit length. The Regge-slope parameter α′ is conventionally defined by T=(2πα′)−1.

String length (ℓs​=α′​)

String tension OurBigBook.com
The characteristic string length is ℓs​=α′​, with T=1/(2πα′). Excited string states have masses of order 1/ℓs​ and higher-derivative corrections become important at that scale.

Regge trajectory (J=α′M2+a)

String tension OurBigBook.com
A Regge trajectory is an approximately linear relation between angular momentum and squared mass. A classical rotating open string obeys J=α′M2, with quantum effects adding an intercept.
